infoText.balanced: Balances carbohydrates, protein, and fat for everyday eating with room for variety. Often easier to sustain long term than highly restrictive patterns. Informational only — not a medical prescription.
infoText.low_carb: Lowers carbohydrate intake while raising the relative share of protein and/or fat. “Low carb” covers a range of carb limits and is not the same as ketogenic eating. Informational only.
infoText.high_protein: Emphasizes protein for muscle maintenance and recovery, especially with resistance training. Suitable amounts depend on body weight, activity, and goals. Informational only.
infoText.keto: A very-low-carbohydrate, high-fat approach aimed at nutritional ketosis. It can be restrictive and is not appropriate for everyone. Individual carb thresholds vary. Informational only.
infoText.atkins: A phased low-carbohydrate approach where allowed carbs can change by phase. This app uses a simplified starting distribution, not every Atkins phase. Informational only.
infoText.paleo: Focuses on minimally processed foods often associated with hunter-gatherer diets and commonly excludes grains, legumes, and dairy. There is no single official macro ratio. Informational only.
infoText.mediterranean: Centers vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, olive oil, nuts, and fish. It is a food-quality pattern, not a fixed macro percentage. Informational only.
infoText.dash: Supports heart health and blood-pressure management with vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and lower sodium. Not defined by one universal macro ratio. Informational only.
infoText.custom: Build your own carbohydrate, protein, and fat split. Match it to your goals and needs — percentages must total exactly 100% to save.
